reconstructed_theorem_text: For every measurable space Omega, every measure mu on it, every natural N including zero, every feature:Fin N->Omega->R, and label:Omega->R, assume MemLp(feature(i),2,mu) for every i and MemLp(label,2,mu). Thus the supplied functions are almost-everywhere strongly measurable and have finite L2 seminorm. Write n=(N:R), r(omega)=n^(-1)*sum_i feature(i)(omega)-label(omega), F_i for the L2(mu) class of feature(i), and Y for that of label. Then r^2 is genuinely Bochner integrable under mu, and integral_Omega r^2 dmu = norm_{L2(mu)}(n^(-1) times sum_i F_i-Y)^2. Both sums run over all N indices in Fin N. Mu need not be a probability measure, finite, or sigma-finite. Chosen representatives of L2 classes equal the supplied functions only almost everywhere; pointwise representative equality is not asserted. At N=0 the sum is empty and real inverse is zero, so r=-label and the conclusion becomes integrability of label^2 and integral label^2 dmu=norm(Y)^2. The feature premise is then vacuous but label membership remains required.
objects: Omega, arbitrary measure mu, natural N, indexed real feature functions, real label, actual scalar residual, and their L2(mu) equivalence classes.
domains: Omega is any measurable space; mu:Measure Omega; N:N without a positivity assumption; feature:Fin N->Omega->R; label:Omega->R. The norm is on real Lp R 2 mu and the integral is a real Bochner integral over all Omega.
quantifiers: For every Omega,mu,N,feature,label, if every indexed feature and label satisfy the stated MemLp premises, both conclusions hold. Each sum quantifies every i:Fin N.
assumptions: The supplied assumptions are L2 membership of each feature and label, including almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite L2 seminorm. No separate squared-residual integrability, mass restriction, or positivity of N is assumed.
conclusion: The squared actual residual r^2 is integrable under mu and its real integral equals the squared norm of (N:R)^(-1) times the sum of the feature classes minus the label class.
scopes: The same mu is used by every premise, toLp construction, integral, and norm. The quotient residual corresponds to the actual residual almost everywhere, not necessarily pointwise through chosen representatives. Fin N has exactly N indices. At N=0 the feature family has no indices and the assertion reduces to the label second-moment identity. L2 membership need not imply L1 integrability of individual functions for infinite mu. The first conclusion ensures genuine integrability in the second.
constant_dependencies: The exact common averaging coefficient is (N:R)^(-1), equal to zero at N=0. There is no unspecified bound, probability normalization, or loss factor 1/2.
